claims.text: TaVCrW is a refractory high-entropy alloy with a disordered BCC solid-solution state.
TaVCrW exhibits short-range order between 2000 K and 2400 K.
Electronic excitation effects near the Fermi level are potentially relevant in TaVCrW.
An MTP trained on TaVCrW DFT data can replace the EAM reference potential.
Free energy perturbation can replace thermodynamic integration for calculating the TaVCrW solid-liquid free-energy difference.
The MTP can accurately reproduce the ab initio phase-space distribution of solid and liquid TaVCrW.
Short-range order stabilizes solid TaVCrW by approximately 2–3 meV/atom.
Electronic gap shifts at the Fermi level are critical to the validity of the FEP approximation.
An accurate MTP provides a computationally efficient surrogate for the DFT energy landscape while retaining SRO and electronic effects.
Sampling the accurate MTP reference state allows FEP to bypass the thermodynamic-integration path.
The MTP-FEP method will reduce computational cost by more than 80% relative to EAM-plus-TI TOR-TILD.
The MTP-FEP solid-liquid free energy will differ from the TOR-TILD result by no more than 0.5 meV/atom.
A supercell containing more than 100 atoms is typically sufficient to avoid artificial periodic constraints on SRO clusters in complex liquids.
The 2000–2400 K interval is the relevant solid-liquid coexistence regime in which SRO stabilization is active in TaVCrW.
Empirical GGA-PBE/LDA underbinding and overbinding rules do not hold for V and Cr at 0 K.
Errors associated with the 0 K DFT treatment of V and Cr could propagate through the MTP training set.
Finite-temperature magnetic fluctuations can contribute to alloy free energies.
Neglecting high-temperature magnetic fluctuations may cause free-energy deviations in TaVCrW if magnetic entropy is significant.
NbMoTaW is a suitable simpler benchmark alloy for isolating the difference between TI and FEP.
The hypothesis is falsified if the free-energy discrepancy exceeds 0.5 meV/atom or the cost reduction is below 80% at the required accuracy.
